status: G4 rest: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-courier-horse, in Chapters III and VII (on the web in Chapter III only)
use: A courier's horse under its saddle cloth, waiting by the courier table in a court beyond the board (Chapters III, VII and XI).

generator.prompt: A Roman post horse of the imperial courier service, mid-3rd century AD, standing square: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head held level and facing forward, tail hanging straight down, symmetrical. A lean bay horse about 1.45 metres at the withers with a black mane and tail and black lower legs, wearing a bronze-studded leather bridle with the reins hanging forward from the bit, and a red woollen saddle cloth with a fringed edge laid over its back, held by a breast strap and a girth. No saddle frame, no stirrups, no rider, no people. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: The second attempt, as asked: a bay with a black mane, tail and lower legs, in a studded bridle with its reins, under a fringed red saddle cloth held by a breast strap and a girth. Kept with a note: its ear tips came tinted the red of the cloth. It came facing its +z and was turned a quarter round: 2.03 m long and 1.8 m to its ear tips. Beside Chapter III's courier table it reads at once, its red cloth the brightest thing in the court.
